newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady, no Buba rate move seen.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady, no Buba rate move seen.

text.p: German call money rates were little changed at 3.05 to 3.10 percent on Monday with dealers confident the Bundesbank will keep its key interest rates unchanged this week.

Dealers said they expected the Bundesbank to set a repo tender at an unchanged fixed rate of 3.00 percent on Tuesday, and to hold rates steady at Thursday's policy-making council meeting, the first after a four-week summer break.
Dealers also all but ruled out the possibility that the Bundesbank may switch to variable-rate this week.
With financial markets as volatile as they are now, it would make no sense for the German central bank to loosen its grip on the money market rate, dealers said.
Economists polled by Reuters unanimously expect the repo rate to stay fixed at 3.00 percent this week.
Commercial banks' deposits at the Bundesbank rose to 42.5 billion marks on Friday from 41.1 billion on Thursday. The average for the month through Sunday rose to 40.5 billion from 40.0 billion marks.
Lombard borrowings totalled about 100 million marks on Friday. The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average (FIONA) fell to 3.09600 percent on Monday from 3.10000 percent on Friday.
